expectation: Nuclear stain in regulatory T cells (CD3+CD4+). They should be uncommon: scattered single cells, enriched in immune infiltrates and lymphoid aggregates or stroma, within CD4+ regions, with most other cells negative.
notes: FOXP3 lights discrete, compact cells scattered across every core and denser in immune-rich cores. Near CD4-dense tissue these cells sit as a sparse subset among CD4+ cells, as Treg should; the background stays dark.
observed: A: sharp single-cell dots in all cores, densest in immune-rich cores, dark background. B and C: a few compact positive cells, the rest negative. D: one bright, slightly elongated cell. E: about 15 discrete FOXP3 cells among CD4+ cells.
why: A sparse, discrete, nucleus-sized population that is enriched in immune areas and sits among CD4+ cells matches a Treg stain, and there is no haze or texture-following.
